reachabilityLines: RTC state (Pokemon Gold (English)): the MBC3 clock's day counter and halt bit select the table. Only days0 and days512 recur boot after boot: after the first boot no other state remains.

A 140-511-day bracket (days200, days260, days300, days450, days700, days780, days850, days1000) lasts ONE boot: the day counter is written back mod 140 by FixDays/SetClock on this boot, so the next boot is in 0-139.

A halted clock (halt-days0, halt-days200, halt-days260, halt-days300, halt-days450, halt-days512, halt-days700, halt-days780, halt-days850, halt-days1000) is a cartridge whose clock was halted and has not been booted since: StartRTC, called at the end of StartClock on every boot (home/init.asm:123 -> engine/rtc/rtc.asm StartClock -> StartRTC: res B_RAMB_RTC_DH_HALT), clears the halt bit unconditionally.
So a prediction in a bracket or halted state is first-boot only, and a typed outcome from a later boot is inverted under the two-state prior (days0, days512).

STRUCTURAL (home/time.asm:110-113, SetClock :205-250, SaveRTC rtc.asm:76-89): the day counter is days since the battery went in (or the last write-back); FixDays writes it back mod 140, so brackets 140-511 are single-boot transients; the carry bit is written back unchanged and cleared only by SaveRTC on a save. A runner who resets repeatedly is, after the first boot, in one of two states only: days0 (the primary table) or days512 (carry, < 140 days). GSE and the community bruteforcer boot with gambatte's fresh clock (0 days, running) = days0.

Dead battery: unmodelled: what a real MBC3's registers read after power loss (halt bit, carry, garbage day count, or nothing) is hardware behaviour the harness does not model; no bracket can be assigned a priori. If the halt bit reads set it is in the halted family; if only the carry, in the days512 family; otherwise in a day bracket; which one can only come from a typed TID (inversion).
